subject: science
title: Animal Homes
about: Where animals live and the home or body part that makes the place fit: gills and fins for water, wings and nests in trees, dens, burrows, lodges, webs and hives, fur for the cold and wide feet for sand (LS.1.1.2). It goes one step past Where Can It Live by naming the part or the home that meets the need.
tip: On a walk, spot an animal and ask two questions: where is its home, and what part of its body helps it live there?

cards.q: A fish has gills. What do gills help a fish do?
cards.note: Gills take the oxygen a fish needs out of the water. People cannot do that.

cards.q: What does a fish use to swim?
cards.note: The tail fin pushes the fish forward. The other fins help it steer and keep its balance.

cards.q: What part of a bird's body lets it fly?
cards.note: Wings and light bones help a bird fly up to its nest.

cards.q: What does a bird use to build its nest?
cards.note: Many birds build nests up in trees, out of reach.

cards.q: A beaver piles up sticks and mud in a pond to make its home. What is it called?
cards.note: Beavers live in North Carolina ponds and rivers too.

cards.q: What does a spider spin to catch its food?
cards.note: A web is sticky silk that comes out of the spider's body.

cards.q: Where do honeybees live and keep their honey?
cards.note: Thousands of bees can live in one hive.

cards.q: A chipmunk digs a hole in the ground to live in. What is the hole called?
cards.note: A burrow keeps a chipmunk safe and snug.

cards.q: Ants dig tunnels and rooms under the ground. What is their home called?
cards.note: The little mound on top is just the door. Most of the home is below.

cards.q: A black bear needs berries, nuts and a den. Which place has all three?
cards.note: North Carolina forests and mountains are home to black bears.

cards.q: A frog has smooth, wet skin and lays its eggs in water. Where does it live?
cards.note: A frog's skin must stay wet, so it stays close to water.

cards.q: A duck has webbed feet. What are they good for?
cards.note: Webbed feet work like little paddles.

cards.q: A polar bear has thick fur and a layer of fat. Why?
cards.note: Polar bears live in the far north where it is icy. White fur also hides them in the snow.

cards.q: A camel's feet are wide and flat. What does that help it do?
cards.note: Wide feet do not sink into the desert sand.

cards.q: What does a turtle carry on its back for shelter?
cards.note: Many turtles can pull their head and legs inside.

cards.q: An owl has very big eyes. When do they help it find food?
cards.note: Owls sleep in the day and hunt for mice at night.

cards.q: A mole has big, strong front paws. What are they for?
cards.note: A mole digs tunnels under the grass and lives there.

cards.q: A deer has long, thin legs. What are they good for?
cards.note: Fast legs help a deer get away from danger.
